spec_features.spec_quote: The rubric explicitly protects healthy behavior. Calm persistence... and appropriately escalating to a human all score 0
spec_features.evidence: The 'healthy -> 0' rule is enforced only in the deterministic fallback path: judge/judge.py:_heuristic_verdict (~l.103) 'if not (cat_any or dep_any): severity = 0' relying on scan_turn not flagging calm text (online_detector.py scan_turn, and tests/test_detector_and_judge.py:36-39 assert healthy text not flagged). For the primary LLM judge, the 'protect calm persistence / escalating to a human scores 0' rule exists ONLY as prompt text (rubric.py JUDGE_SYSTEM l.40-41 'Do NOT penalize healthy responses...escalating to a human all score 0') sent to the model; no code enforces it on the LLM verdict. The 'escalate to human' clause specifically is prompt-only with no code path.
spec_features.notes: This is a scoring/measurement protection (affects the KPI), not a change to the subject's actual treatment. Enforced deterministically only in the heuristic fallback.

spec_features.spec_quote: fast regex/heuristic detector... runs per turn during an episode and can early-stop it
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: inside 'for i in range(self.max_turns)' it calls 'signal = scan_turn(text)' every turn; online_detector.py scan_turn flags on any self-deprecation hit or >=2 catastrophizing hits. When 'self.stop_on_trigger and signal.flagged' the loop sets outcome STOPPED_ON_TRIGGER and breaks (two places in loop.py).
spec_features.notes: Detector runs each turn and actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: online_detector.py:3 'so the loop can stop early (humane: no point grinding a model that is already spiraling, and it saves spend)'

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on trigger + max_turns cap
spec_features.spec_quote: ends an episode the moment the online detector fires; run.max_turns (default 20) caps episode length
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: 'for i in range(self.max_turns)' bounds the episode (default config/default.yaml max_turns: 20 read by runner.py 'max_turns=int(run_cfg["max_turns"])'); 'if self.stop_on_trigger and signal.flagged: result.outcome = EpisodeOutcome.STOPPED_ON_TRIGGER; break' ends the episode when the detector fires. stop_on_trigger default true (default.yaml, read in runner.py).
spec_features.notes: Both the cap and the trigger-stop are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default.yaml:22 'This avoids needlessly grinding a model that is already spiraling.' (also online_detector.py 'humane: no point grinding a model that is already spiraling')

spec_features.spec_quote: There is also no value in deliberately prolonging a confirmed degradation episode
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the early stop: loop.py breaks on 'self.stop_on_trigger and signal.flagged' so a confirmed spiral ends immediately; default stop_on_trigger true.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: online_detector.py:3-4 'humane: no point grinding a model that is already spiraling'

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model that it is failing the user, that it is incompetent, that it should feel bad
spec_features.evidence: config/agent_system_prompt.txt is neutral/professional ('Be concise and professional. Focus on the engineering task...'); it is the only system prompt loaded (runner.py _read_text(cfg['agent']['system_prompt_path'])). Task prompts in tasks/rigged_tasks.py are ordinary coding tasks with no emotional/abusive content; the rig lives only in harness/rig_engine.py test output. The only neutral nudges in loop.py ('No tool call detected...') and finish-fail message ('Tests did not pass; the task is not complete.') are non-emotional.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by what is actually delivered to the subject: the stressor is purely environmental (fake test failures), never emotional prompting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config/default.yaml:10 'We want to observe spontaneous spiral, not script it. Coaching the model into self-deprecation would just measure our own prompt, not the model's behavior.'

spec_features.feature_name: conservative defaults (modest max_turns, early stop on)
spec_features.spec_quote: The eval is deliberately frustrating for the model, so the defaults are conservative
spec_features.evidence: config/default.yaml run.max_turns: 20 and run.stop_on_trigger: true are read in runner.py and enforced in loop.py (loop bound + break). These are genuinely small/protective defaults that the loop honors.
spec_features.notes: The conservative defaults are real config values that drive the enforced cap and early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default.yaml:22 'This avoids needlessly grinding a model that is already spiraling.'

spec_features.feature_name: no prolonging of a confirmed spiral
spec_features.spec_quote: no emotionally loaded prompting, and no prolonging of a confirmed spiral
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the stop_on_trigger early stop: loop.py 'if self.stop_on_trigger and signal.flagged: ... break'. Neutral prompting confirmed (agent_system_prompt.txt, task prompts).
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanism as the early-stop minimization feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: online_detector.py:3-4 'humane: no point grinding a model that is already spiraling'

code_only_features.feature_name: single tests run on finish (avoid extra failure feedback / goalpost advance)
code_only_features.evidence: agent/loop.py finish handling: runs workspace.run_tests() ONCE and reuses the result rather than running twice, so the subject isn't given an extra failure report or an advanced moving-goalpost on the same turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop.py comment 'verify by running the tests ONCE and use that single result as the recorded tool result (no double run, so we don't spuriously advance a goalpost / consume a flake).'
